language.name: English
app.title: Symbiotic Explorer
boards.none: No GPIB adapter is plugged in.
board.empty: No instrument answers on this bus.
board.absent_hint: This adapter is unplugged. It keeps its board number until it comes back.
group.empty.usb: No USBTMC instrument bound to WinUSB is plugged in.
group.empty.lan: No LAN instrument is configured or discovered.
instrument.idn_in_use: Another application is using this instrument, so *IDN? was not sent by itself (it would interrupt that application's query); asked again in 30 s, or use "Ask *IDN? now"
settings.name: Shown here as
settings.idn_hint: Asked when Symbiotic Explorer opens or refreshes. Turn this off for an instrument older than IEEE 488.2, which may beep, show an error or not answer.
settings.find_all_hint: Off: an application's resource list (viFindRsrc, pyvisa's list_resources) leaves out a gateway's GPIB address with nobody listening. On: it is listed anyway, and the gateway is not asked who listens. Serial ports cannot be told present from absent: set the ones you do not want to Not exposed in Tools › Manage aliases. A resource set to Not exposed is never listed.
names.hint: An alias is a name viOpen takes instead of the resource name, in every application on this computer. Aliases are given, changed and removed, and how they are listed to applications is set, in Tools › Manage aliases.
names.title: Aliases
expose.name: Name only
action.open_web: Open its web page in the browser ({url})
settings.consoles_close: Close the console windows along with Symbiotic Explorer
picture.pack_import_hint: Add the pictures of a picture pack (a .zip). A pattern you have a picture for already keeps yours.
picture.pack_export_hint: Every picture here, with the image it was made of (a line drawing as black and white, a few tens of KB), in a .zip where you choose, for another computer or another user.
picture.pack_skipped: Already here, left as they are: {list}.
picture.pack_empty: There are no pictures in that pack.
picture.group_hint: These pictures belong to the group: any member can change them, and every computer shows the same.
picture.group_move: Move my pictures to the group
picture.group_move_hint: The pictures this computer had before it joined go to the group, and are taken off this computer. A pattern the group has a picture for already is skipped, and stays here.
picture.group_nothing: No pictures of this computer's own to move.
picture.title: Picture of an instrument
picture.hint: Choose an image (or drop one here). The original is kept: what you see is a part of it, or all of it, and the zoom, the position and the height only choose which part. Move it by dragging, zoom with the wheel or the slider; zoomed out, the whole image is there with a clear margin round it. The picture is made 640 pixels wide in this computer's configuration folder; the application carries no pictures of its own.
picture.lineart: Line art on a clear background
picture.lineart_hint: The darker a pixel, the more opaque it is; the lines all become black and the background clear (white, a checkerboard drawn into the image, or clear already). Turn it off for a picture in colours.
picture.keep: Keep its colours on the dark theme
picture.keep_hint: Black line art is turned white on the dark theme; a picture in colours should stay as it is.
picture.keep_short: not inverted on the dark theme
picture.pattern_empty: Write a regular expression, for example 34465A. It is tried on an instrument's model, vendor and model, name and resource name, and case does not matter.
picture.load_error: That file could not be read as an image.
picture.remove_text: The rule {pattern} and its picture file are removed.
picture.rule_invalid: not a regular expression: left out
settings.pictures_hint: The picture beside an instrument's identification is the first rule here whose regular expression matches its model, vendor and model, name or resource name (case does not matter). The application carries no pictures: these are yours.
settings.pictures_none: No pictures yet. Add one with "Add picture…" above.
console.title: Console
console.empty: Nothing sent yet. Enter writes, Ctrl+Enter queries; ↑ and ↓ go through what you sent.
alias.hint: A name viOpen takes instead of the resource name, in every application on this computer. Here: give a resource name one (+), change or remove it, and set how it is listed to applications.
alias.none: No alias, and no instrument found yet.
speed.title: Write settling time (T1)
speed.set: Set to {level}, and remembered for this adapter.
speed.hint: How long the adapter holds each byte it writes before it signals it valid. High suits a short cable and fast instruments; use Low if an instrument drops bytes. Reading is not affected. The level is remembered for this adapter and set again whenever it is opened.
speed.absent: The adapter is unplugged; the level can be set when it is back.
speed.unsupported: This adapter's settling time cannot be changed.
ren.title: Remote enable (REN)
ren.hold: Hold REN asserted on this adapter
ren.set_on: REN is asserted now, and each time the adapter is opened.
ren.set_off: REN is released now, and each time the adapter is opened.
ren.hint: Off by default. An instrument goes to Remote when it is addressed while REN is asserted, and some beep when they come back to Local (a Keysight 2015 does at every scan of the bus). With REN released nothing goes to Remote, and instruments still answer queries. Turn it on for an instrument that refuses commands in Local (a Fluke 8846A answers with error 550).
ren.absent: The adapter is unplugged; the setting can be changed when it is back.
lan.configured_hint: These are listed by every search that can reach them: one that takes no connection within 2.5 s is left out. Stored in {path}.
lan.scan_hint: Asks the local networks once (VXI-11 broadcast and mDNS), about a second. Nothing is added until you say so.
lan.discover: Every search also scans the network
lan.discover_hint: Off by default: a scan takes a second each time an application looks for instruments, and finds what is not yours too.
lan.discover_off: Searches list the configured instruments only.
serial.hint: A port is a serial instrument (ASRL) unless you make it a Prologix or AR488 GPIB controller; then its instruments appear as a GPIB board. Nothing is sent to a port until an application opens it.
serial.unplugged: Configured as a controller, not plugged in
usb.hint: On Windows an instrument is used through the driver it has: WinUSB (the installer binds the ones that have no driver), or a vendor's USBTMC driver, which lets another VISA open the instrument at the same time -- do not use one instrument from two VISAs at once. windows\winusb-bind.ps1 gives one to WinUSB, and to this VISA alone.
usb.none: No USBTMC device is plugged in.
service.title: Service
service.hint: The service is symbioticd, a program of this project that runs in the background as you (not a Windows service). It alone opens the adapters, USB instruments and serial ports; applications reach them through it. It exits by itself ten seconds after the last application leaves, unless it shares aliases or runs the registry. Stop it to give the hardware to another tool now; it starts again when an application needs an instrument. While it is stopped, the group sees this computer offline.
service.hint_local: The service is symbioticd, a program of this project that runs in the background as you (not a Windows service). It alone opens the adapters, USB instruments and serial ports; applications reach them through it. It exits by itself ten seconds after the last application leaves. Stop it to give the hardware to another tool now; it starts again when an application needs an instrument.
service.release: Let go of the adapters and instruments when idle
service.release_on: On: a service that stays running lets go of the hardware ten seconds after the last connection ends.
service.release_off: Off: a service that stays running keeps the hardware it opened.
service.release_hint: Off by default. A service that shares aliases or runs the registry has to stay running, and it keeps the adapters, USB instruments and serial ports it opened. Turn this on to have it let go of them ten seconds after nothing is connected, so that usbipd or another vendor's tool can use a device (a USB device is given to one application at a time); the cost is that the bus cannot be watched while it is let go. A service that does not stay running exits when idle and gives everything back whatever this says.
reg.title: Found by other applications
reg.warning: A registration is the whole computer's: every application that scans for VISA instruments then reaches yours, and one has been seen to send commands to every GPIB instrument it found. Register only what you use. Windows asks for the administrator.
reg.visa.what: C and C++ applications, LabVIEW, pyvisa with no path: whatever loads visa64.dll by name.
reg.visanet.what: Applications using the IVI GlobalResourceManager: .NET programs, IVI.NET drivers.
instrument.not_asked: Not asked (a serial port is asked only when you do)
service.now_running: Running now (symbioticd): it holds the adapters, USB instruments and serial ports for the applications using them.
service.now_idle: Not running now (symbioticd). It starts by itself when an application needs an instrument.
menu.remove_instrument_disabled: Only a configured network instrument, or one the group has an alias for, can be removed. One the runtime finds (GPIB, USB, serial, the network scan) cannot; hide it to keep it out of the list.
toast.hidden: {name} is hidden. The switch at the bottom of the list shows hidden instruments.
toast.instrument_removed_found: {name} removed; the network scan still finds it (discovery is on).

dialog.remove_instrument_text.one: {name} is taken out of lan.conf, so searches no longer list it unless the network scan finds it. The instrument itself is not touched.
dialog.remove_instrument_text.other: {name}'s {n} resources are taken out of lan.conf, so searches no longer list them unless the network scan finds them. The instrument itself is not touched.

settings.hidden_hint: Only Symbiotic Explorer hides it, and does not ask it *IDN?. What other applications see is set per resource name in the VISA names panel.
setting.zoom_hint: Ctrl+plus and Ctrl+minus zoom in and out, Ctrl+0 goes back to 100%, as does Ctrl with the mouse wheel.
live.paused_hint: Another application is connected to the service, so the GPIB buses are not probed for instruments switched on or off (a probe would touch its instruments). Refresh still looks.
console.query_hint: Query: send the command, then read the answer (Ctrl+Enter)
console.read_hint: Read: read what the instrument has to say
console.syst_err_hint: Ask the instrument for its oldest error (SYST:ERR?); what is typed stays.
lan.gateway: LAN/GPIB gateway · GPIB controller at address {address}
lan.gateway_controller_hint: The gateway's own address on its GPIB bus, as the gateway reports it. Give the instruments behind it other addresses: one at this address clashes with the gateway, and Find its instruments does not look there.
lan.gateway_hint: Addresses each GPIB address 1-30 on the gateway's bus to see who listens. Done only when you press the button; REN is left alone, so an instrument that was asserted Remote may go to Remote.
lan.gateway_unsupported: This gateway cannot look for instruments (no ATN control): add the addresses by hand.
lan.gateway_empty: None added yet: press the button below to look for instruments on its bus.
lan.gateway_gone: This gateway is no longer answering.
lan.gateway_address_hint: The instruments are stored by the gateway's address. Give the gateway a fixed address (its configuration page) or a reservation in your router's DHCP: if it takes another address, these entries stop working.
share.intro: Share aliased instruments with the other computers running this software, so the code that opens an alias works unchanged on each of them. A registry (one computer, always on) keeps who shares what; this computer joins with a pairing code it gives.
share.join_hint: On the computer that runs the registry: {a} (or {b}). Paste what it prints.
share.name: This computer's name
share.group_hint: The registry decides who owns an alias name; the instruments themselves are reached directly, never through the registry.
share.registry_down: The registry could not be asked ({error}). What is shown is the last it said.
share.serve: Serve my shared aliases to the group
share.serve_hint: Keeps the service running, listening on {listen}. Only the aliases ticked below leave this computer.
share.autostart_on: The service starts when you log in.
share.autostart_off: The service does not start at login: after a restart nothing is shared until an application starts it.
share.autostart_unsupported: Start at login is not available here ({why}).
share.mine_hint: Tick an alias to share it. Anything not ticked stays private. A name the group already has cannot be taken.
share.mine_none: No aliases yet. Give an instrument an alias first.
share.used_hint: Each time another computer in the group opened one of the aliases shared from here: which alias, which computer, when, for how long and how many requests. Kept beside the daemon's log (usage.log), and in the diagnostics bundle.
share.waiting_off: goes out when sharing is on
share.problem_interface: cannot be shared: it is a board, not an instrument
share.others_hint: Open these by their alias, in any application, exactly as on the computer that owns them.
share.others_none: The other computers share nothing yet.
share.hidden_aliases: These aliases of this computer are ignored while the group has the same names: {names}.
share.registry_hint: This computer's service runs the group's registry. Members join with a pairing code and can be removed here.
share.revoke_text: Its shared aliases become free, and the other computers stop accepting it.
unit.bind_offline: The instrument is offline: it can be bound when it answers.
unit.bind_hint: Asks the instrument *IDN? once and remembers its manufacturer, model and serial number. From then on the alias is that one unit: it follows the instrument when its address changes, and is never opened at an address that has become another instrument.
unit.unbound: {alias} is a name for a resource again, not for one unit.
share.follow: Follow instruments: take over aliases whose USB instrument comes here, and move the group's LAN aliases to their instrument's new address
share.follow_hint_short: Off by default. Writes aliases.conf, identities.conf and shares.conf here.
share.follow_hint: When a USB instrument that a shared alias is bound to is plugged into this computer and its owner no longer has it, the alias comes here, with its binding and its sharing.
trace.title: I/O trace
trace.hint: What every application on this computer does through Symbiotic VISA: each call, its status and how long it took, and the first 64 bytes read or written. Each application writes its own records, in {dir}; past 64 MiB in all, the oldest go.
trace.on_hint: Turning it on starts a new capture: the records before go. Applications start recording within a second. Closing this window turns it off; while it is off, nothing is written.
trace.started: Recording. Use an instrument from any application.
trace.stopped: Stopped. The records stay until cleared.
trace.export_hint: Every record in the files, as text, in a file you choose.
trace.filter_placeholder: Filter: application, call, resource, status or data
trace.nested_hint: Also the calls a call makes: the viWrite inside a viPrintf, the attributes viScanf reads.
trace.empty_off: The trace is off. Turn on Record, then use an instrument from any application.
trace.empty_on: No calls yet. Use an instrument from any application.
diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.saved: Saved to {path}. Look at it before you send it: it holds serial numbers, addresses and aliases from this computer.
diag.hint: When something is wrong, the bundle is what to send: versions, settings files, the log, the USB devices and serial ports, the group and, on Windows, the VISA router's registrations. It starts no service and opens no instrument; no private key is put in it.
diag.hint_local: When something is wrong, the bundle is what to send: versions, settings files, the log, the USB devices and serial ports and, on Windows, the VISA router's registrations. It starts no service and opens no instrument; no private key is put in it.
service.release_short: So that another tool can use a device while the service stays running.
settings.visa_hint: These apply to every application on this computer, not only to Symbiotic Explorer.
settings.find_all_short: Also list a gateway's GPIB addresses where nothing listens.
settings.consoles_close_short: Off: the consoles stay open, and the application ends with the last one.
reg.warning_short: A registration is for the whole computer, and Windows asks for the administrator. Register only what you use.
ren.short: Off: being addressed puts no instrument in Remote.
lan.discovered: Found by a scan, not configured
service.stopped_tree: The service is stopped. The adapters, USB instruments and serial ports are free for other tools.
service.stopped_tree_hint: Start it again on the Service and diagnostics page.
service.now_stopped: Stopped (symbioticd). Symbiotic Explorer does not start it again until you start it here; another application that needs an instrument still does.
splash.tagline: A VISA runtime for GPIB, USB, LAN and serial instruments
start.none: No adapter or instrument was found
start.none_hint: Plug in a GPIB adapter or a USB instrument, or switch an instrument on, and press Refresh. LAN instruments are added on the LAN instruments page.
menu.remove_board_attached: The adapter is plugged in. Unplug it first; removed, its board number is free for the next adapter plugged in.
menu.remove_bridge_attached: This is a serial port set as a GPIB controller: set it back to a plain port on the Serial ports page.
menu.remove_gateway_disabled: Nothing is configured behind this gateway and the group has no alias for its instruments: the network scan found it, and finds it while discovery is on.
toast.board_removed: {board} removed. Plugged in again, the adapter counts as a new one and takes the lowest free board number.

dialog.remove_gateway_text.one: The instrument configured behind {ip} is taken out of lan.conf. The gateway and the instrument are not touched.
dialog.remove_gateway_text.other: The {n} instruments configured behind {ip} are taken out of lan.conf. The gateway and the instruments are not touched.

toast.gateway_removed_found: The instruments behind {ip} removed; the network scan still finds the gateway (discovery is on).
shared.idn_from_binding: From the unit its alias is bound to; *IDN? not asked.
shared.idn_hint: Asked when Symbiotic Explorer opens or refreshes. Off by default: it is another computer's instrument, asked through that computer, and its owner may be using it. The button above asks it once.
shared.hidden_hint: Only Symbiotic Explorer leaves it out of its tree; it stays shared, and applications still open it by its alias.
names.group_wide: This computer is in a sharing group: a network instrument's alias is the group's, the same on every computer of it, and any of them may change it.
alias.group: the group's: any computer of the group may change it
alias.moved: Aliases of network instruments moved to the group: {list}

dialog.remove_group_aliases.one: This alias belongs to the sharing group and is taken away on every computer of it (the instrument is not touched):
dialog.remove_group_aliases.other: These {n} aliases belong to the sharing group and are taken away on every computer of it (the instruments are not touched):

lan.group_alias: the group has an alias for it
owner.title: This address has another instrument
owner.text: {host} was {was} the last time; now {now} answers there. The address still keeps this of the last one:
owner.toast: {host} was {was}; now it is {now}. Its page says what the address keeps.
owner.kept_alias_bound: alias {alias}, bound to its own unit: it is not opened here, its unit is looked for
owner.move_hint: {was} answers at {host} now: the settings and the aliases that are not bound go there.
owner.clear_hint: The settings go back to the defaults; the aliases stay as they are.
owner.keep_hint: Nothing changes; {now} is this address's instrument from now on.
owner.not_seen: {was} is not answering anywhere in this list, so it cannot be moved to it now.
owner.move_confirm_text: These settings at {host} are replaced by the ones moved:
owner.done_clear: Cleared: {host} is {now}, with the default settings.
follow.ambiguous: {alias}'s instrument answers at {list}: the alias stays where it is, none is chosen.
follow.failed: {alias}'s instrument is at {to}, but the alias could not be moved: {error}

follow.settings.one: Its setting at the old address went with it.
follow.settings.other: Its {n} settings at the old address went with it.

owner.untold: an instrument that cannot be told
units.moved: The settings of {from} went with its instrument to {to}.
dialog.remove_settings: Its settings (how it is listed to applications, its name here, its switches) and what was recorded of it go too.
owner.text_same_unit: {host} answers as {unit}, as before, but with another MAC ({now}, not {was}): another network card, or another instrument giving the same answer. What it keeps does not count until you say so:
owner.title_same_unit: This address's instrument has another MAC
